### Results

Every performed evaluation returns one value of the core result algebra,
directly or as a refined value mapped into it (P5):

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `satisfied` | the declared predicate holds on the exact basis |
| `falsified` | a declared counterexample defeats it |
| `indeterminate` | the available admissible evidence cannot decide it |
| `out_of_frame` | the evaluation requires an undeclared material relation or capability |
| `invalid_basis` | the subject or basis cannot support the evaluation |

This core is the only one. Results of constraints, judgments, frame
evaluations, stops, work steps and effects are stated in it or in a
refinement mapped into it, so that results from any members combine under
one rule ([Conjunction of results](#conjunction-of-results)). Purpose and
material relation: no combination can report success while a failure, an
undecided question, an unperformed evaluation or an uncertain effect
remains, and none of these can be mistaken for another (P5, P6).

Recording. A result records its core value together with the predicate
evaluated and the original domain outcome, which is the refined value
where a refinement produced it. A mapping into the core never owns domain
meaning: the member, profile or adopting Product that defines the refined
value keeps it, and a consumer that needs the domain distinction reads the
domain outcome, never the core value alone (P1, P6).

Standing. The standing of a result is what it establishes about its
predicate; it is distinct from the standing of a commitment (§1). Only
`satisfied` establishes the predicate. `falsified` establishes that the
predicate fails and names the counterexample. `indeterminate`,
`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` establish neither, and each names what
would decide: the evidence, the missing relation or capability with its
owner where the subject gives one, or the basis repair. By support for the
predicate, `satisfied` stands above each other value, and the other four
are not ordered among themselves.

No refinement or mapping raises a result's standing (P5, P6):

- a falsified or failed result never maps to a satisfied or successful one;
- a result that admissible evidence cannot decide never maps to
  `satisfied`;
- an evaluation that was not performed stays distinct from one whose
  evidence cannot decide: it has no
  [closed result](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse), and it is never mapped
  to `indeterminate` or to any other core value;
- an effect whose completion is unknown never maps to no effect or to
  completed.

Not performed. An evaluation that is required or planned and was not
performed has no closed result; an actor cannot report an evaluation it
did not perform (P6). Nothing is coerced to success: a failed,
indeterminate, out-of-frame, out-of-scope or invalid-basis result follows
the declared result algebra and returns its own value under it, never
`satisfied`, and a missing result, being no result, enters every
conjunction over it as a gap: a planned assessment without a closed result
where an assessment was planned, and uncovered coverage where none was.
This
conserves
[RF-012](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#rf-012-closed-results),
whose five values the table restates unchanged, and
[AC-007](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-007-constraint-and-refusal),
whose rule that a failed, missing, indeterminate, out-of-scope or
invalid-basis result follows the declared algebra rather than being
coerced to success is the sentence before; both are restated here once.
[REFERENCE_FRAME §3](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-012-closed-results) states
RF-012 as a law over frames and
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §4](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-007-constraint-and-refusal)
states AC-007 as a law over constraints; each uses this core and neither
defines it again.

Refinements. A member, profile or adopting Product that needs finer
outcomes defines a refinement. The refinement names the question it
answers and the predicate its mapping is for, and maps every refined value
to exactly one core value. No outcome exists outside the core; a
refinement adds no core value and keeps the pressure of `indeterminate`,
`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` explicit. Where a refined value would
map to one of two core values according to its cause, the cause is part of
the refined value and each resulting value maps once (P5, P1). A further
refinement, by a member, profile, project or adopting Product, may split a
refined value by cause. The parent-value rule governs every such split:
each child value names its parent value and its cause and keeps its
parent's core value; a child that needs a different core value needs a
different parent value, which only the owner of the parent declares; and
no child takes `satisfied` from a parent that is not `satisfied`. No
further refinement raises a result's standing (P5, P6, P1). Purpose and
material relation: a consumer that reads a parent value reads the same
core value from each of its children, so a split by cause adds a domain
distinction and never changes what the parent establishes (P5, P6). The
refinements for admission, activation and steps are
[ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition); each other
member, profile and adopting Product states its mapping where it defines
its values.

Availability, assessment and acceptance are separate results, each with its
own predicate: that a step produced a candidate; that the candidate meets
its declared criteria; and that the
[decision owner](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation) accepts it at its
boundary. A step having produced a candidate never maps to the candidate's
fitness or acceptance, and acceptance is never inferred from a successful
step (P6; [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition),
[EVALUATION §4](EVALUATION.md#4-review-results) and
[§5](EVALUATION.md#5-acceptance)).

Out of frame or indeterminate. The boundary between these values is drawn
on what the activated frame declares and on what the step did with it (P5,
finite capacity and graceful total handling; the material relation drawn
is the three-way out_of_frame boundary: capability not declared, capability
declared and exercised, capability declared and not exercised; rc.2 RF
#rf-012-closed-results). Three cases; the first two name core values, and
the third names none:

- `out_of_frame` when the claim requires a material relation or an
  evaluator capability that the activated frame does not declare. The
  result names the missing relation or capability, its owner where the
  subject gives one, and the reconfiguration pressure it creates
  ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement); rc.2 RF
  #reconfigure-when-necessary). A term the claim depends on and the frame
  leaves undefined is an undeclared material relation: its meaning can
  alter the result and it enters through no declared input (rc.2 RF
  #material-relation, RF-003; P1). Whether the step exercised anything is
  irrelevant to this value; the ground is the missing declaration.
- `indeterminate` when the available admissible evidence cannot decide the
  claim (rc.2 RF-012). The result names the evidence that would decide, as
  its residual uncertainty (rc.2 RF #return-a-closed-result). Where the
  claim also depends on an undeclared relation or capability,
  `out_of_frame` and `indeterminate` each have a lawful ground; the result
  names the value it returns and that ground, and this boundary excludes
  neither (P5).
- no value of its own when the step did not exercise a declared capability
  the evaluation requires. A result is returned wherever a sufficient
  evaluation or an applicable judgment exists without that capability,
  identifying its evidence, verdict and residual uncertainty like any
  closed result (rc.2 RF #rf-012-closed-results, #return-a-closed-result):
  a counterexample found by what was exercised, as when source inspection
  falsifies A in a claim of A and B, returns `falsified`, and common
  agreement cannot discard it (rc.2 RF #result-conjunction). Where none
  exists because the capability was not exercised, the evaluation was not
  performed and has no result: the step's stop state carries it,
  `incomplete` under
  [construction availability](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability), and
  its work state ([ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart))
  carries the unexercised capability as a residual (P6). In either case
  the unexercised part, B above, has no result: in every conjunction over
  it, it is a planned assessment without a closed result, and the known
  failure A survives with it ([Conjunction of results](#conjunction-of-results)).
  The evaluation's result and the step's stop state answer different
  questions, so the step's stop value never becomes the evaluation's
  result.

### Conjunction of results

Conjunction combines results into one result for a composite predicate: a
claim made of component claims, a decision over several evaluations, or
the outer contract of composed steps. It is defined here once, over the
core. A member or profile that combines results applies this rule and
declares only the choices it leaves open (P4a, P4b, P5, P6). Purpose and
material relation: failure, undecidability, non-performance and uncertain
effects stay distinct after combination, so a composite can neither report
success nor hide which kind of gap it has while one of them remains in
what it requires.

A conjunction takes three inputs and keeps them apart:

1. the closed results returned, each a core value with its predicate and
   domain outcome;
2. the planned assessments that have no closed result applicable to the
   composite: evaluations the composite requires that were not performed,
   or whose result is absent, stale, bound to another subject or basis, or
   incapable of establishing its claim;
3. the required coverage that no planned assessment addresses: for a
   required obligation set R and the coverage C that the planned
   assessments admit, the uncovered coverage R minus C.

Gaps. A conjunction with any item in the second or third input is never
`satisfied`. Its record names which kind of gap it has, not performed,
uncovered or both, and each item. An uncovered obligation is never
reported as satisfied or as an omitted planned assessment; a planned
assessment without a closed result is never reported as uncovered or as an
`indeterminate` component.

Stale results. A held result is stale for a composite when the basis it
binds is not the basis the composite requires of that component, because
a later state has superseded or advanced it or because it binds another
subject or basis (§2, Basis). Two questions stay apart, so that one
composite has one reported value (P3, P5, P6):

- an evaluation performed on a subject or basis that is stale, advanced,
  ambiguous or mismatched against the one it must bind returns
  `invalid_basis` for its own predicate, or is reactivated on the current
  basis; [RF-005](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates)
  states this law over frames, and a conjunction that receives that
  `invalid_basis` holds it as a returned result;
- a component whose only held result is stale has no closed result
  applicable to the composite: on the basis the composite requires, its
  evaluation was not performed. It is a planned assessment without a
  closed result, in the second input, and a gap. Its stale value is
  neither counted as a returned result nor relabelled `invalid_basis` for
  the composite, and it stays in the record with its own basis;
- the declared basis relations disagree (Reported value below) only among
  returned results, each bound to the basis the composite requires of it,
  whose bases the declared rule requires to agree or to join in a coherent
  composite basis, and which do not.

A stale `satisfied` never counts toward the composite. Purpose and
material relation: answering one stale component as a gap in one place and
as `invalid_basis` in another would give one composite two reported
values; keeping the evaluation's own value apart from the composite's gap
keeps the reported value unique and the stale result visible.

Survival. Every known failure (a `falsified` result with its
counterexample), every planned assessment without a closed result and
every uncovered obligation is carried with the composite and survives every
join: combining conjunctions takes the union of known failures and of
planned assessments without a closed result, and recomputes uncovered
coverage over the combined obligations. A known failure and a gap of
either kind survive every join. Common agreement among contributors
cannot discard a constraint or a material counterexample that only one
contributor found. A missing, wrong-subject, conflicted or indeterminate
mandatory result stays unresolved under the declared rule, and aggregate
satisfied status cannot replace it (P4b, P5).

Predicates travel. Each component keeps its predicate and domain outcome
through every join, so an uncertain effect stays distinct from a failure
and from an undecided claim, and a `satisfied` for one predicate never

### Constitutional chain

```text
Goals → Intent → Product Definition → Requirements → Design → Code
  → Events → Projection → Delta → Scenarios → Gap analysis
  → Repricing, new Goals or Intent
```

Goals define the current overriding concerns for the active body of work.
Intent defines purpose and direction. Product Definition defines the current
product realisation of the mutable source project, its key terms and its
end-state shape in terms that can be decomposed into requirements.
Requirements define invariant truths the system must satisfy. Design
defines the structural decisions, interfaces, carrier surfaces and delivery
topology that make those truths achievable; ADRs are one durable form of
design record, not a second constitutional layer above design. Code
realises those decisions. Events record what happened. Projection
reconstructs current truth from the event stream. Delta reveals drift
between intended truth and realised state. Scenarios test operational
meaning: whether the system can do what the words describe. Gap analysis
identifies where real use cases hit the current model and reveal
insufficiency. Repricing updates goals, intent, product, requirements,
design or code when the system no longer harmonises; when gap analysis
reveals constitutional insufficiency, it generates new goals or intent (P2,
P1; rc.2 #constitutional-chain).

This is the homeostatic loop. Every link is load-bearing. A break at any
link, goals with no downstream repricing path, an unowned requirement, an
ungrounded design record, code without a design decision, creates
accidental law (P6).

The goals surface is the bounded work-wave surface: it captures the current
overriding concerns for the next body of work, keeps temporary focus out of
deeper constitutional layers until it is intentionally repriced there, and
is more immediate than intent while remaining higher-level than product
definition and requirements. The product-definition surface is the bridge
between direction and obligation: it states the current product definition
of the mutable source project in present-tense terms, names the product
terms and boundaries that downstream layers rely on, and provides the
surface that requirements decompose. It is not the immutable release cut
and not the installed product; those are the lineage objects of FOUNDATIONS
§2 (P3).

Requirements are the constitutional what of the project. They are not
limited to user-visible features: the live requirement surface may include
capabilities, invariants, constraints, governance and verification
obligations; what matters is that each requirement states something the
project must make true. Design is the structural how: it chooses the
concrete realisation that satisfies requirement truth, interfaces, topology,
file placement, carrier documents, entry and control surfaces, runtime
wiring and lawful tenant boundaries. Requirements may require such surfaces
to exist and be delivered; design chooses where and how they are realised
unless the path itself is constitutional (P2, P1).

The relation between the WHAT and the build tenants that realise it is
[§11](#11-build-tenant-binding) (P2).

### Design rule

Requirements state what control or delivery surfaces must exist; design
decides the concrete mechanism that realises them. If a technology stack,
carrier or runtime is not already constrained by an upstream constitutional
surface, choosing it is part of design, not a separate upstream authority
(P2, P1; rc.2 #design-rule). A tenant's choice of stack, human process or
combination is its execution binding, declared in that design under §11.
The boundary matters especially for
agent-facing bootstrap and control surfaces: requirements may say that
authoritative bootstrap or control surfaces must be present, carry bare
axioms and route to the canonical method; design decides whether those
surfaces are entry documents, embedded blocks, standalone compiled
artifacts or another lawful topology (PRODUCT_DEFINITION §12). If
filenames and placement are hardcoded in requirements without
constitutional necessity, the requirement surface has absorbed design
detail and made re-derivation harder.

### Realisation shape

For a realisation boundary that the design profile governs (DESIGN_MODULE,
tier 3, adopted under its own adoption rule), the core rule is: semantic
steps should read as transforms over admitted truth; effects should be
explicit and pushed to the edge. If a reader has to inspect orchestration
code, mutable workspace state, service methods or fallback defaults to
determine what the system means, the design is too imperative and too
coupled (P1, P6; provenance rc.2 DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD #3-core-rule).

Non-goals of that profile (P1, P4a; provenance rc.2
DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD #17-non-goals): it does not require one specific programming language,
elimination of all imperative code, monadic or category-theory vocabulary,
or replacing every exception with a custom algebraic type. It does require
that the implementation shape remain readable, modular and honest about
where meaning lives and where effects happen. Where a boundary composes
higher-order functions or effectful computation, it does require an
explicit composition and effect algebra with its applicable identity,
closure, cardinality, effect and authority-conservation laws (FOUNDATIONS
§4 Composition). The vocabulary is optional; the law is not.

### Universal intake triage

There is one front door for substantive change. The intake label does not
determine the process class: a reported bug, feature request, issue,
regression, operator finding, release blocker or scenario failure all enter
through the same intake triage (P2, P6; rc.2 #universal-intake-triage).

Intake triage determines six things: whether the report represents a
substantive change at all; the affected product boundary and intended
scope; the lawful change class; the lawful re-entry point into the
constitutional chain; the downstream surfaces and evidence that must be
repriced, re-derived or re-proved; and whether the work remains within the
currently declared release scope or requires repricing of that release
plan. No bug, feature, issue or other intake bypasses this triage by going
straight to code, tests or release handling. The purpose is not a separate
tracking bureaucracy; it is to classify impact correctly so the change
enters the method at the right constitutional boundary.

Triage triangulates a failure across the applicable reference frames over
the same subject and basis. Each frame tests candidate diagnoses against
its material workspace variables, governing relations and evidence; their
combined results constrain the supported cause, preserve unresolved
alternatives and uncertainty, and identify the smallest sufficient lawful
scope of repair. The frame that exposes a failure need not contain its
cause. Repeating the same analysis under different frame names supplies no
additional causal evidence. The smallest sufficient applicable frame
configuration is used, under frame applicability and frames in conjunction
(REFERENCE_FRAME §5 and §6). The frames' results combine under the one
[conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results): each
keeps the diagnosis it evaluated as its predicate, a counterexample that
one frame finds survives the join, and a frame planned and not applied
leaves its diagnosis open, never ruled out. Counterexample localisation
applies where required (ASSURANCE; provenance rc.2 STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE
#counterexample-localization). This prescribes no reviewer count and no new
review round; required independence stays intact. A diagnosis grants no
repair effects and does not establish that governing meaning must change: a
candidate may instead need correction under sufficient existing law (P6).

### Computed classification and treatment

Intake supplies one reusable classification result rather than requiring
each role to reconstruct the same facts (P4b, P6, P1; rc.2
#computed-classification-and-treatment). Three annotations keep the kinds
of determination apart: C denotes reproducible facts and declared rule
application; J denotes residual semantic or materiality judgment; O denotes
a ruling reserved to its actual owner. The annotations grant no authority,
an instance of
[FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What
creates no authority, and introduce no calculus kind, runtime, classifier interface or mandatory
document.

The explicitly selected source, worksite or qualification capability
produces C over the exact request and desired outcome, the known targets
and effects, the operation grant and work lifetime, the product definition
and governing basis, the baseline and the available candidate, the declared
relations, the accepted design and trace bindings, the evidence and the
applicable rules. Its output identifies the producer and procedure
revision, the inputs, the result, the scope, the source routes, the
reproduction relation, the unknowns and the invalidators. A missing
candidate or missing evidence is an input state, not a claim that nothing
changed.

The computed result exposes four things, in this order:

1. Authority traversal. Follow the explicit source, ownership, dependency,
   composition and projection declarations from the affected targets and
   effects. Identify each reached layer and owner, its exact basis and its
   changed, unchanged or unknown relation, the traversed edges and the
   unresolved frontier. Include root, authority and grant changes even when
   public bytes are equal. An absent edge does not prove irrelevance;
   undeclared or semantically uncertain materiality remains J.
2. Public delta. Enumerate the complete relevant serialised member universe
   under its owning declaration and applicable projection, including helper
   and generated dependencies. Report added and removed identities and
   every retained member with changed typed value or bytes, with exact
   before and after values. A rename is removal plus addition unless its
   owner supplies an identity-preserving relation. A missing candidate,
   incomplete enumeration, ambiguous identity or unavailable projection
   leaves the affected delta unknown; membership equality alone proves no
   value equality (P3).
3. Accepted-design coverage. Join changed bytes and relations to explicit
   accepted scope, traces and acceptance evidence. Distinguish covered,
   missing, stale, ambiguous and outside-scope evidence. A filename, listed
   artifact or digest alone establishes no accepted coverage. Current trace
   coverage is a computed fact; residual semantic sufficiency remains J.
4. Rule-determined treatment. Apply only declared rules with sufficient
   input facts, recording their owners, matched predicates and
   consequences. Expose the smallest lawful re-entry, the next action, the
   applicable evidence or assessment, the reserved ruling and the carrier
   lifetime, with any conflict or missing premise still unresolved. A label
   or filename cannot select the route. When rules settle the question, no
   residual judgment is invented.

The values these steps assign, a relation changed, unchanged or unknown,
an identity added, removed or retained with a changed value, and evidence
covered, missing, stale, ambiguous or outside scope, are facts of the
computed result. They are not results of an evaluation and map to no core
value. An evaluation that consumes them returns its own core value with
its predicate under [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), and
an unknown it consumes stays unknown. Purpose and material relation: a
classification fact is never combined as an evaluation result, so
evidence classified covered, or a relation classified unchanged, cannot
stand in for a `satisfied` result (P5, P1).

A public delta or other nonconformance does not itself require changing

authorised outcome, the candidate is rejected or locally repaired within

Unknown treatment withholds dependent reliance or promotion, not unrelated

be silently treated
as no effect, and is reconciled as ACTIVATION §5 states before any retry

A new role, conversation or resumption reuses valid C after checking exact

## 11. Build-tenant binding

This section owns the relation between a product's WHAT and the build
tenants that realise it: what a tenant binds, what stays fixed while it
chooses, and what its evidence shows. It applies to every product built
with this method (P2, P1, P6).

Terms used in this section:

- A build tenant is one independent, project-owned HOW realisation of a
  product's WHAT. The build-tenancy context of
  [PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#8-what-how-and-work-carriers)
  names it, and the product definition's tenant registry locates each one.
- The requirements calculus of a product is the set of obligations its
  WHAT states, the outcomes it permits, and its rules for refining and
  composing the work that realises it.
- A computational calculus is a declared set of executable operations,
  with the laws by which they compose, the transformations they permit,
  and their effects and resource behaviour, as far as these are material
  to the obligations.
- An execution environment is the concrete means that performs those
  operations: a technology stack; a human process, made of people, roles,
  documents, communication channels and decision procedures; or a
  combination of the two.
- A tenant's build-tenant binding has two parts: its calculus binding,
  from the requirements calculus to its computational calculus, and its
  execution binding, from that computational calculus to its execution
  environment. A tenant's registry entry locates the tenant; it is not the
  binding.
- Author identity and actor identity are as
  [EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment) defines them:
  authorship is one condition of an assessment's independence there, and
  an actor's identity is not an authority.
  Operation kind is what an operation does, such as construct, assess,
  relay, record, measure or decide, together with the authority that kind
  of operation requires.

Rules:

1. Realisations of one WHAT. One WHAT is realised by one or more
   independent build tenants, whatever the physical layout. The WHAT is
   constitutional and each tenant's realisation is HOW; a tenant-local
   realisation stays derivative until its governing truth is ratified in
   specification (§2). Each tenant binds the product's requirements
   calculus to a declared computational calculus and binds that calculus
   to a concrete execution environment. Both bindings are that tenant's
   design and realisation: they are declared in its existing design and
   realisation surfaces, chosen under the Design rule (§2) and recorded as
   design decisions (§10), and the method requires no further carrier. The
   tenant owns its binding, its realisation and their evidence; the WHAT
   keeps its meaning (P2, P6).
2. Selection. The execution environment may be a technology stack, a
   human process or a combination. Its selection stays within the
   requirements calculus, including every human decision that calculus
   requires: no choice of environment removes a required human decision or
   a required independent assessment. Author identity, actor identity and
   operation kind stay distinct, and none determines another. Who authored
   a tenant does not select its environment; one actor may perform
   operations of several kinds, each under its own grant; and an actor's
   identity neither decides the kind of an operation nor grants authority
   for it. A person performing an operation does not by that make it human
   adjudication: §5 states the admission that makes an operation human
   adjudication and how a person who decides under policy without it is
   governed. The same holds for every decision the requirements reserve to
   a human: the person the governing authority admits for it takes it, and
   a person's part elsewhere in the process does not (P6, P1).
3. Material content. For the obligations it serves, the binding
   identifies:
   - the operations, each with its inputs, outputs, effects and outcome
     values; each outcome value maps to exactly one core value under
     [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), and an intended
     external effect, one of uncertain completion included, is recorded as
     [ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects) states;
   - the composition laws, and the transformations the calculus permits;
   - the resource measures;
   - the operational assumptions on which conformance depends, among them
     those about actors, tools, availability and failure.

   Human effort, elapsed time, communication and machine resources are
   measured where a selected obligation needs them. Each measure states its
   unit and its boundary: what is counted, and where measurement starts and
   stops. A resource claim without its unit or its boundary supports no
   conformance claim. The size of a selected context is measured as
   [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope)
   step 3 measures it, against the capacity the binding declares for the
   actor. The law for declaring, measuring and honouring resource limits
   is [ACTIVATION §6 Resource limits](ACTIVATION.md#resource-limits), and
   this rule binds it: the values of a step's time, spend and other
   resource limits, and the units and boundaries the environment can
   measure, are those of the execution binding, stated before the
   activation they limit. Where a configuration states its resource limits
   and its assumptions about failure
   ([ACTIVATION §1 Configuration](ACTIVATION.md#configuration)), it takes
   them from this binding (P0, P2, P5).
4. Conformance evidence. The obligations of the requirements calculus
   decide fitness; the kind of executor alone neither accepts nor rejects a
   realisation. Evidence establishes how the bound realisation satisfies
   the required meaning and constraints, including the applicable
   authority, independence, failure and recovery conditions. Conformance is
   judged under
   [EVALUATION §6](EVALUATION.md#6-conformance-of-realisations), and two
   conforming tenants need not behave identically outside the contract.
   Each assessment returns a core value for its predicate, and the tenant's
   conformance is their
   [conjunction](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results), with the
   obligations of the requirements calculus as its required coverage. A
   convenient stack never weakens an obligation. An execution plan that
   merges two required independent assessments, or substitutes an
   automated result for a required human decision, is a counterexample to
   the obligation it weakens, so the binding's conformance for that
   obligation is `falsified`; in any run under such a plan the lost
   assessment or decision has no applicable closed result. Matching
   outputs, lower cost or a faster run do not discharge the lost
   independence or authority. A claim that a binding preserves categorical
   structure is a further claim: it meets the Formal fragment of
   [FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra) and stays distinct from
   conformance on the equivalence ladder of EVALUATION §6 (P6, P1, P4b).
5. Reuse. A computational calculus may be reused across tenants and
   execution environments wherever each binding satisfies its laws, and
   each binding shows that it does. A different language, tool, team or
   person does not by itself require a different calculus: replacing the
   executor of an operation while the calculus's laws hold changes the
   execution binding, not the calculus (P1, P4a).
6. Representation. A representation of the requirements calculus or of a
   binding in a_c, the axiomatic calculus of
   [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md), prescribes no executor and
   does not establish execution conformance by structural validation alone
   ([AC-018](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-018-structural-and-semantic-separation)).
   An a_c model of a human process that passes structural validation
   neither selects an automated executor nor shows that the process meets
   its requirements; execution conformance needs its own evidence under
   rule 4 (P1, P6).

### Configuration

A configuration allocates a task's responsibilities and information
exchanges to frames; activation binds an actor to each frame (§2). It
spans the task's work. The active frame configuration of
[FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#frame-objects) is the part of it used for
one evaluation or decision (P0, P6).

Allocation. The allocation is derived from the task's operations, the
dependencies among them, the capabilities of the available actors and the
required assurance. These conditions constrain a configuration without
determining it. One frame or several, fixed or adaptive allocation, a
hierarchy, peer coordination, or an arrangement that changes as actors
allocate work within their contracts may each be adequate. The method
prescribes no role inventory, hierarchy, coordinator or actor sequence
(P0, P2; [RF-016](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-016-implementation-neutrality)).

Explanation. The design that selects a configuration explains its
allocation, including the material resource limits it assumes, such as
context, attention, time and spend, each declared as §6 Resource limits
states, and its assumptions about failure. The
explanation is recorded in the existing design, frame declarations and
work records; no separate configuration carrier is required. It is
proportional (§6): for a direct entry, the intake states it, its
capability envelopes carrying the resource limits and its stale,
out-of-scope and re-entry conditions the failure assumptions (P2, P6).

Direct entry. A one-frame configuration is lawful. One directly
authorised task that fits a sufficient frame may be entered directly, as
Roles and delegation below states, subject to any separately required
assessment (P0, P2).

### Roles and delegation

Roles are relations over steps that a configuration allocates
(Configuration above), not kinds of actor and not a fixed inventory.
Where a configuration's operations include construction, assessment or
disposition, this member names the responsibility for each: a
constructor owns the bounded implementation and its self-review; an
assessor evaluates a frozen candidate independently; a decision owner
disposes. A configuration may allocate other responsibilities. Where
independent assessment supports promotion, the assessor evaluates the
exact live subject, its authority paths, proof and installed state, not
the constructor's summary (EVALUATION §3). This preserves the
independent-review relation and prescribes no actor count: one actor may
occupy different roles across different claims when independence for the
assessed claim is preserved; no role name confers an operation
([RF-016](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-016-implementation-neutrality);
P6; provenance rc.2 SPEC_METHOD #construction-assessment-and-delegation).

The governing authority relation declares whether a bounded proxy may
accept and advance routine actions. Inside a step, a proxy so declared may
accept preservation, require local repair, reject a violating candidate
and advance to the next already-authorised action; what it cannot change,
and the re-entry such a change requires, is the proxy limit of
[FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), which
this paragraph applies and does not restate. Human ceremony is not
required at every transition when the governing basis, the affected cone,
the decision envelope and the re-entry conditions are already accepted;
this delegation does not weaken direct human acceptance where the
governing product or release law requires it (P6).

When one capable context has sufficient existing work authority, exact
intake and operation grant, it may enter directly as constructor. No
coordinating activation is required solely to appoint that constructor.
The applicable configuration (Configuration above) selects
coordination when material contexts, authority, capability or required
independence need it; a role or frame name alone does not create that
need. Direct entry preserves
execution-contract admission (Admission above), the smallest lawful
carrier, the required assessment and the reserved decisions; it permits
bounded work and condition-based result recording, not self-acceptance at a
boundary owned elsewhere (P0, P6).

Recording a result without review. Where the applicable law requires no
independent assessment and reserves no acceptance, the constructor that
holds the grant may record the satisfied bounded result, with the conditions
it found satisfied and their evidence, in the existing durable result
surface (Admission above), without adding a carrier, coordinating
appointment, review or recreated design view solely to mark completion. The
recording waives no condition that actually applies, states only
conditions that were evaluated, as an actor cannot report an evaluation it
did not perform
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Not performed), and is
no disposition at a boundary owned elsewhere
(§3 Disposition). Where an assessment or a reserved acceptance does apply,
it stays required, and an insufficiency found during the work withholds
the dependent effect and returns the question to its owner. Carriers and
profiles refer to this paragraph and add only their own carrier binding
(P0, P2, P6; provenance rc.2 SPEC_METHOD
#construction-assessment-and-delegation). Purpose and material relation:
requiring a review or a ceremony that no law requires adds reasoning cost
without removing ambiguity (§6), while recording a satisfied result where
a review or acceptance is required would read construction as acceptance.

One bounded operation grant may cover its declared construction, status and
checkpoint sequence. Actual role transitions are recorded in the existing
work carrier; a status change alone requires neither a new grant nor
rehashing an unchanged subject. A material change to the operation, the
subject, the territory, the authority or the validity conditions requires
the affected binding to be resolved before effect. Where the selected
configuration restricts its coordinating role from mutation, as the
executive configuration (Configuration above) restricts its Executive,
the restriction that the coordinating role mutates nothing remains
applicable; an operation grant covering the sequence does not lift it
(P6, P3).

### Effects

An effectful step's intended external effect has one of three values,
mapped for the predicate "the intended effect occurred", that is, the
declared outcome of the effect is attained. The value turns on what the
admitted evidence establishes about that outcome (P5 with the open-world
premise, P6):

| Value | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| `completed` | satisfied | evidence about the subject establishes that the intended effect occurred in full and that the effect has ended |
| `not_effected` | falsified | evidence about the subject establishes that the declared outcome is not attained and that no later completion of the effect can attain it, for example where no effect began, the effect ended short, an interval that the declared outcome bounds has closed with part of it not done, or the part already done has itself made the declared outcome unattainable, as when it destroyed what the outcome needed; any part that did occur is named with the value |
| `completion_unknown` | indeterminate | neither of the other values is established: the evidence cannot decide whether the intended effect has occurred or will occur, as for a request whose response was lost with no counterexample observed; or the evidence shows the intended effect in full while the effect may still be acting, and the outcome stays undecided until what the effect leaves on the subject is settled; its residual names the observation that would decide |

`not_effected` requires evidence about the subject. A lost response, an
absent record, or an actor's context that holds no trace of the effect is
not that evidence, and the value stays `completion_unknown`.
`completion_unknown` never maps to `completed` or to `not_effected`.

Whether the effect has ended is a second question beside the predicate
above, and it enters the value only as a conjunct of `completed`. An
effect has ended where evidence about the subject establishes
that it no longer acts on the subject or that it never began. Where an
effect began and the evidence does not establish its end, the end is not
established, and that is recorded beside the value as a residual naming
the observation that would establish it. The end never decides a
`not_effected` value and is never folded into one: when an interval that
the declared outcome bounds has closed with part not done, the value is
`not_effected` while the effect may still be acting. The residual does
not weaken the counterexample, and the counterexample does not resolve
the residual. `completed` alone requires the end established, so a
counterexample stands without proof that the effect has ended, while
success is never claimed for an effect that may still be acting
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Standing).

An effect of uncertain completion is one whose value is
`completion_unknown`, or whose value is `not_effected` with its end not
established. §5 reconciles it, sufficiently for the next dependent
action, before any repetition or dependent action. A `not_effected`
value licenses neither treating the effect as absent nor repeating it
while its end is not established.

The refinement is new. Its material relation is whether an action whose
external effect may have occurred is repeated or relied on; §4 names a
lost post-effect response as a case that no added core value solves, and
this refinement records it in the existing core. Keeping the end of the
effect beside the value keeps two facts that one value would merge: a
counterexample already established for the declared outcome, and an
effect that may still be acting.

## 5. Work state and restart

Work state is the tuple of: the current persistent workspace; the governing
basis; the applicable closed results and judgments with their invalidators;
the residuals; and the known uncertainty over external effects. It is an
object (P3); its carrier (files, an event stream, another admitted owner) is
a profile or realisation choice.

Resumption is re-entry of the same method over the current work state,
starting from the current material state, by a possibly different actor.
It recovers applicable progress, re-checks the invalidators of each reused
result (§7), reopens only affected support, and reconciles uncertain
external effects, sufficiently for the next dependent action, before any
repetition or dependent action. Resumption does not imply idempotence: an
action whose external effect may have occurred is not repeated blindly;
the lawful next moves are reconciliation, yield or stop.

Checkpoint. Acceptance binds one exact checkpoint. The next
already-authorised bounded action may begin without renewed human approval;
acceptance does not widen the selected outcome or the affected relation set
(P6, P2). A preservation checkpoint may retain unfinished or unaccepted
work under an existing exact operation grant; it identifies its parent or
predecessor, the included territory, the concurrent-writer disposition and
the durable evidence location, and it is neither acceptance, promotion nor
publication. A proposed restart, which reconstructs from less than the
retained work, identifies why repair of retained work is insufficient,
which obligations and evidence survive, and which causal assumptions
change; reconstructability alone does not select reconstruction. Conserves
[UP-020 checkpoint and continuation](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#checkpoint-continuation-progress-and-churn);
the generic work-state object, the reconciliation of uncertain external
effects and the non-idempotence rule are new (P0, P5 with the open-world
premise).

Progress is accepted material movement toward the selected outcome;
prerequisite work names the obligation it enables; preservation and
repeated proof are evidence, not new progress; rejected or superseded
construction is churn; discovering previously hidden distance revises the
forecast and is not negative progress. Paperwork, code volume, test count,
commit count and review count are not progress by themselves. These are
semantic categories, not a numeric progress algorithm; a consumer may
derive its own progress and churn projections from them (P2). A member,
profile or project that distinguishes finer categories for its own
outcome states them as a refinement of these, naming this paragraph and
mapping each of its categories to one of progress, prerequisite work,
evidence that is not new progress, churn or forecast revision; a category
it cannot map is a change to this owner, not a parallel category (P2, P6).

proceeds from unreconstructable context; if a constructor's report
substitutes for required independent live evidence; if a bounded proxy
changes a governing relation outside its delegation; if unrelated
incompleteness blocks a closed causal cone; if a same-process test is used
to prove materially cross-process authority (§7); or if rejected activity

### The workspace and an actor's account

The workspace and its authoritative inputs persist across activations and
are the continuing truth surface of the work: the surface whose current
material state decides what the work has and has not done. An actor's
context is an account of that state. It is bounded, because it is a
projection of the state (§2); revisable, because an observation can
correct it; and disposable, because a step records its closed results and
step-produced facts before it returns (§1 Admission; P4b). An account is
never a second truth surface, and no later activation needs a prior
actor's context: its intake reconstructs the governing relations without
it (§1 Intake) (P0, P3, P6).

Acquisition ([§2](#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope)) observes the
current subject and its authoritative inputs. Where they materially
disagree with a cached belief, a retained summary or a prior result, the
actor reconciles the disagreement: current evidence corrects the account,
and what the evidence cannot decide stays an explicit unknown. A stored
belief, a summary or a successful prior result never overrules contrary
current evidence. A prior result is relied on only after its
applicability and invalidators are checked against the current subject
and inputs (§7). The actor corrects its account within its grant; where
resolving the disagreement needs an operation, a territory or a decision
outside the grant, the step stops with `re_entry_requested(authority)`,
naming the owner of what it needs (§3 Construction availability) (P5,
P6).

Discarding an actor's private context resets nothing: the workspace, the
applicable valid work and the outstanding obligations remain as the work
state records them. A missing trace in a context, a memory or a summary is
no evidence about the subject. It shows neither that work was not done
nor that an external effect did not occur, nor that it ended; an effect
of uncertain completion keeps the value `completion_unknown`, or its end
stays not established beside its `not_effected` value, until evidence
about the subject decides it (§3 Effects) (P5).

Work that an interruption left partly written is part of the current
material state from which resumption (above) starts, and is assessed as
it stands; an assessment that was not performed has no result and is
never recorded as performed
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results); §3 Construction
availability). The method imposes no universal reset and no obligation to
replay the complete history. The recovery contract that applies, which is
the resuming step's intake with the work state, determines which
observations and which effect reconciliations the next dependent action
needs. Handoff between actors is by closed results, which carry no private
working context and keep their validity and independence conditions (§7)
(P0, P4b).

Purpose and material relation: finite context (P0) means an actor's
context ends or is replaced while the work continues, and discarding it is
safe only because the step-produced facts the outer contract needs are
recorded (P4b). Treating the account as the truth surface would let a
stale account overrule the workspace; treating a discarded account as a
reset would erase progress or repeat an effect that occurred (P5, P6). The
material relation is whether a decision relies on an account that current
evidence contradicts, or reads a missing record as undone work or an
absent effect. This subsection is new in this corpus. The workspace, the
work state and the closed results carry it, and no further carrier is
required.

## 7. Closed result and reuse

A closed result identifies the frame and its activation, the subject, the
basis, the evaluation, the actor, the evidence, the verdict, the residual
uncertainty and the invalidation conditions (the minimal shape is
REFERENCE_FRAME §13). The frame's internal working context need not be
transferred when the closed result and its provenance are sufficient for
the consuming decision; it may still be attached, for audit or otherwise,
without changing the result. Independent evaluations may share valid
mechanical evidence under the declared independence conditions of
[EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment), which owns that
permission (P4b, P0; rc.2 RF #return-a-closed-result).

A closed result is reused by an unchanged consumer that checks exact
applicability; a role, conversation or resumption change alone invalidates
nothing. An invalidator invalidates the affected result before reliance,
even where the subject's own bytes are unchanged, preserving its
predecessor/successor relation and any demonstrably independent surviving
results. The invalidators are three:

- a material input change: a change to the result's subject or to an
  input it rests on, including the admissible evidence that bears on its
  predicate; newly acquired or changed admissible evidence is such a
  change when it is material to the result as
  [FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology) defines material, that is,
  when it could change the result's value;
- a changed basis: a change to any coordinate of the basis the result
  binds (FOUNDATIONS §2, Basis);
- a declared revising observation: an observation that the result or
  judgment itself names as one that would revise it, once it occurs.

### Upward propagation check

Triage consumes the computed classification of

the declared owner and layer traversal, the complete relevant public
membership and value delta, the accepted-design scope and trace coverage,

behaviour and remain sufficient for the authorised outcome. Their presence
proves no coverage. Missing or ambiguous evidence leaves the affected
treatment unknown; it is not proof that the governing layer itself is
absent (P6).

The re-entry rule is SPEC_METHOD §4's: the
[change classes](SPEC_METHOD.md#change-classes) with their re-entry
points, and the smallest lawful re-entry that step 4 of

exposes, with the paragraph after the four steps: a candidate's public

refines that rule into an upward walk from the realised surface that
checks each layer and stops at the highest layer found missing or

| the governing requirement is missing or insufficient | `requirement_reprice` | re-enter the requirement's owner |
| the requirement is sufficient, and the realising design is missing or insufficient | `design_reframe` | re-enter Design |
| an actual upstream Goal, Intent or Product change | `goal_reprice`, `intent_reprice` or `product_reprice` | follow the change to its owner rather than stopping at a familiar file |
| the current requirement and accepted design suffice, and the implementation deviates | `realization_refactor` | repair or reject the candidate |

Unresolved meaning remains J and a reserved choice remains O, as that
paragraph states (P2, P6).

### Triage metadata

Because tickets are the durable authority surface for work tracking, a
ticket for substantive work carries the minimum metadata required by the
intake triage of [SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#universal-intake-triage):
the declared `change_intent`, the lawful `change_class`, the lawful
`re_entry_point`, and when triage occurred in `triaged_at` (P4b, P2; rc.2
#triage-metadata). The recorded values are those intake triage declared
(Change class and Upward propagation check above).

### Condition-based closure and reuse

A work claim is complete only when every applicable declared obligation is
satisfied by valid evidence for its exact subject, basis and scope; every
required judgment and owner ruling is present and applicable; and no active
non-closure condition remains. A mandatory obligation whose applicability is
unknown, or whose evidence is insufficient, withholds the dependent claim;
evidence presence alone is not satisfaction. The existing owner decides any
reserved acceptance (P6, P5; rc.2 #condition-based-closure-and-reuse).
This condition is the
[conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results) with the
declared obligations as required coverage. This section owns the
closure condition of a work claim;
[SPEC_METHOD §4 Consistency gate](SPEC_METHOD.md#consistency-gate)
applies it as the gate over a declared change span.

Review evaluates these conditions; its occurrence is not the closing event.
Where applicable law requires no independent review or reserved
acceptance, a work claim is recorded as
[ACTIVATION §1 Roles and delegation](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation)
states in Recording a result without review, with the ticket as the
existing carrier. The conditions that still apply include sprint-close
law (§3) and the design profile's law (P6, P2).

An unchanged obligation reuses valid applicable evidence and recorded J
and O under the reuse rule of
[ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse). For a work
claim, the changed material inputs and revising observations that rule
names include a material counterexample, changed evidence and a stated
revising observation of a recorded J; with a changed basis, each
invalidates the affected claim and its dependent results before further
reliance. An unrelated observation is retained as bounded repricing input;
it does not reopen a satisfied claim or expand the work automatically.
Closure recording preserves the exact evaluated scope, the satisfied
conditions, the evidence and the remaining residuals (P4b, P2).

## 4. Review results

A review returns one core result
([FOUNDATIONS §4, Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)) for each declared
predicate it evaluated, with: the exact subject and basis, the evidence
consulted, the findings ranked by consequence, each finding's evidence and
the smallest bounded correction, the residual uncertainty, and the
invalidation conditions. A declared predicate the review planned and did
not evaluate has no result (FOUNDATIONS §4, Results). The review names it
as not performed and reports no core value for it, neither
`indeterminate` nor `falsified`, so that conjunction keeps it apart from
an undecided predicate and from required coverage that no planned
assessment addresses
([FOUNDATIONS §4, Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results);
P5, P6). It may recommend a disposition
([ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)), which is
evidence only and never a disposition; it does not apply one. A finding
without evidence a consumer can chase is commentary.

### Result and triage projection

Where a review returns findings with technical triage, the triage is the
assessor's evidence-bound assessment of each finding against the exact
evaluated claim and basis. Severity, the assessor's grade of consequence,
is evaluation evidence. Priority, the effect on the current promotion
boundary and the disposition are the decision owner's (ACTIVATION §1,
Roles and delegation; when a finding can block is
[§5, When a finding blocks promotion](#when-a-finding-blocks-promotion))
and stay distinct values even where a
Product-defined policy maps one to another. A recommended disposition
is evidence for the decision owner: it is not a disposition, a
priority or a boundary effect, and it is never adopted mechanically (P6,
RF-007). The fields of a triage are declared by the profile that adopts it, and
the scales it uses are bound by the adopting Product (P2, P6; provenance
[reviewer result and triage projection](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE.md#reviewer-result-and-triage-projection)).

The projection of the finding-level triage payload is total over the core
values of [FOUNDATIONS §4, Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). A predicate
not performed has no result and so no triage payload; the payload class
`indeterminate` never stands for it. The payload classes `complete`,
`indeterminate` and `not_applicable` classify the triage only; they are
not new results, dispositions, priorities or lifecycle states (P5, P1).

| Core result | Finding and triage payload | Decision-owner consumption constraint |
|---|---|---|
| satisfied | an explicit no-finding state; triage `not_applicable`; evidence, residuals and invalidation stay present | priority and boundary effect are `not_applicable` to this result unless another exact consumed result supplies a finding |
| falsified | one or more exact findings; triage `complete` where supported, keeping `indeterminate` fields where evidence cannot close them | apply the Product-owned priority and boundary policy without mapping severity mechanically to a disposition |
| indeterminate | a partial finding or observation state; triage `indeterminate`; the exact evidence gaps and residual uncertainty | keep the uncertainty or reactivate a capable evaluation; do not consume it as satisfaction or as a closed finding |
| out_of_frame | the evaluated claim needs an undeclared material relation or evaluator capability; triage `indeterminate`; the missing relation or capability and the exact reconfiguration pressure are named | refine or reconfigure a capable activation and keep the claim unresolved; do not consume the result as satisfaction or falsification |
| invalid_basis | a basis failure; triage `not_applicable`; invalidation evidence and basis-repair pressure | refuse to consume the result and return through the declared basis re-entry relation |

An adjacent observation outside the evaluated claim does not replace the
claim-relative result. The assessor returns it separately, with triage
`not_applicable` to that claim and the exact repricing or re-entry
pressure; the decision owner returns it to its declared owner without
creating a claim-relative block, or another review round, from its
severity alone (P6, P2).

The assessor returns to the decision owner, not to the constructor. It does
not edit the candidate, direct the repair or authorise continuation (P6,
§3).

Purpose and material relation of this projection's generality: the
predecessor stated it for the Reviewer and the Executive only. Stating it
for any assessor and decision owner gives every configuration the same
separation of severity, priority, boundary effect and disposition, and
EXECUTIVE_BASELINE keeps the Reviewer and Executive instance (P6).

### RF-012 Closed results

Every performed evaluation of a frame returns one closed result in the
frame's declared result algebra: the core algebra of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), or a refinement mapped
into it under that section. That section owns the five core values
(`satisfied`, `falsified`, `indeterminate`, `out_of_frame` and
`invalid_basis`), their meanings and the rules over them: that nothing is
coerced to success; that a refinement adds no core value, keeps
indeterminate, out-of-frame and invalid-basis pressure explicit and raises
no result's standing; and that an evaluation not performed has no result,
its stop state being
[ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition). This law
applies them to every frame and defines none of them (P5; rc.2
#rf-012-closed-results).

### Result conjunction

A declared decision rule consumes the closed results of several frames.
The rule, what it must state, and the conjunction it computes are
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
over the core values of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results);
this member defines no conjunction of its own. The outcomes of `conjoin`
map to the core as §5 states (P4a, P5, P6; rc.2 #result-conjunction).

### AC-007 Constraint and refusal

Each constraint names its governed subject, predicate, judgment kind,
latitude and refusal (§3, Constraint). The judgment of a constraint
returns one value of the core result algebra of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), directly or through a
refinement that the owning signature declares and that maps each of its
values to exactly one core value. Under the no-coercion rule of
FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, a failed, missing, indeterminate, out-of-scope or
invalid-basis result of a constraint follows that algebra and is never
coerced to satisfied (P5, P6; rc.2 #ac-007-constraint-and-refusal). The
core values, the rule that no mapping raises a result's standing and the
boundary among out_of_frame, indeterminate and an evaluation that was not
performed are FOUNDATIONS §4 Results'. This law applies them to the
judgment of a constraint and to the outcomes of the operations of this
member, and adds no core value.

Constraint results. The outcomes of a constraint's judgment map for the
predicate "the constraint's predicate holds for its governed subject on
the exact basis" (P5, P6):

| Outcome | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| holds | satisfied | the judgment establishes the predicate on the exact basis |
| failed | falsified | a counterexample defeats the predicate; the judgment names it |
| indeterminate | indeterminate | the admissible evidence cannot decide the predicate; the judgment names the evidence that would decide |
| out of scope | out_of_frame | the predicate is asked of a subject or relation outside the constraint's declared `applies_to`, context or scope, so deciding it needs a relation the constraint does not declare; the judgment names that relation, with its owner where the subject gives one |
| invalid basis | invalid_basis | the subject or basis cannot support the judgment; the judgment names the basis repair |

A missing result is no value of this refinement: a judgment that was not
performed has no closed result, is never `indeterminate`, and enters every
conjunction over it as a planned assessment without a closed result
(FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Not performed).

# PROFILES

Tier 3. Owns the boundary between the core and the profiles, the
declared-binding rule and the import rule that every profile applies
(§1), and indexes the profiles (§2 to §6). A profile is a domain or
operational specialisation of the method; the members of tiers 1 and 2
are the core.

## 1. The boundary

The core names no runtime, no carrier and no executor. Terms owned outside
the core, by a profile, a realisation or an rc.2 member, never enter tier
1 or 2 except in a disposition table: graph, edge, vector, ledger, event
log, worksite, HoG, Markov overlay, screen, entity cut, and the design
profile's IACS and Prime. The traversal record and the functor kinds F_D,
F_P and F_H are tier-1 calculus terms owned by AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5, and
"module" is a generic term, as the predecessor's generic testing law uses
it; neither is restricted here. A profile may bind a core mechanism to one of these;
the binding is declared in the profile with its direction, preserved
meaning, narrowed scope and invalidation. The declared-binding rule is new
(P0 boundary, P1); its shape follows ODD's specialisations of F_P and F_H,
which [ODD §5 Probabilistic compute](ODD.md#probabilistic-compute) owns in
the graph-native context and carries as their provenance; the
predecessor's section is rc.2
[ODD probabilistic compute](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/ODD_METHOD.md#probabilistic-compute).

Import rule. A profile imports the generic families of tiers 1 and 2 that
its rules rest on, and owns only its own bindings: the terms and choices
it adds for its domain or operation, among them the declared bindings
above (P1, P6). It imports each concept it uses from a member of tiers 1
and 2 under
[FOUNDATIONS §2 Imports between members](FOUNDATIONS.md#imports-between-members),
which states what an import is, and restates none of that member's rules.
Its family table, in the format of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law),
names each imported family by its ID and the section that holds its table,
in the premise column; the profile's rules rest on that family's
consequences, with the standing FOUNDATIONS §3 gives them, and the
family's rules and choices keep their owners. A profile that refines
another profile declares the refinement in its lead; the refined profile
keeps its rules, and the refining profile owns only what it adds (P1, P6).
The import rule is new in this corpus. Purpose and material relation:
each profile table cites the families it rests on without restating them,
so no generic rule gains a second owner in a profile and no choice a
profile adds is presented as following from the foundations (P6, P1).

A worked application, a hello world or a data mapper is an external test
subject; its particulars cannot become generic method functionality by
precedent.

# WRITING_GUIDE

Guide. Owns the practical writing discipline for this method's surfaces:
the core rule, style rules, habits to remove, the marks of good and bad
prose, alignment of tone with the authority layer, practice for
specification artifacts, the layer checks and present-tense writing of the
current surface. Consumes [SPEC_METHOD §2](SPEC_METHOD.md#2-the-chain)
(the chain, its layers and the specification surface rule) and
[§6](SPEC_METHOD.md#6-lineage-and-release) (the release version boundary),
and [POSTING_GUIDE](POSTING_GUIDE.md) (the commentary layer); defines none
of them. Every clause names the principle that requires it (P0 to P6,
FOUNDATIONS §3). A route written `rc.2 #anchor` is into
`stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/WRITING_GUIDE.md` and is provenance
only; nothing here depends on that cut to be applied.

## 1. Core rule

Write for a reader who is technically fluent and short on time (P0; rc.2
#core-rule).

State the claim. State the reason. Remove the performance around them
(P2).

## 2. Style rules

Provenance rc.2 #style-rules.

1. Prefer direct positive statements over contrast framing (P1).
2. Remove setup paragraphs that announce what a section will say (P2).
3. Use concrete nouns and verbs, not motivational or promotional
   language (P1).
4. Keep one claim per sentence when possible (P1, P6).
5. Prefer precise technical vocabulary over vague intensifiers (P1).
6. Use an example only when it reduces ambiguity (P2, P1).
7. Do not write filler transitions whose only purpose is tone (P2).

## 3. Habits to remove

Remove these habits (P2; rc.2 #remove-these-habits):

- "not X, but Y"
- "simply"
- "just"
- "clearly"
- "obviously"
- "powerful"
- "robust"
- "seamless"
- "game-changing"
- generic reassurance
- dramatic phrasing

They usually add tone and no information (P2).

## 4. Good prose

Good prose on these surfaces is factual, bounded, explicit about
authority, explicit about uncertainty and easy to challenge (P6, P4b;
rc.2 #good-prose).

A sentence that sounds polished and carries no new constraint or
observation is cut (P2).

## 5. Bad prose

Bad prose on these surfaces (P6, P1; rc.2 #bad-prose):

- implies conclusions instead of grounding them;
- repeats one claim in different words;
- mixes current reality with target intent without labelling the
  difference;
- explains basic concepts to an expert audience; or
- turns straightforward instructions into brand language.

## 6. Tone and authority layer

Method documents should sound constitutional. Requirements should sound
normative. Design should sound structural. Commentary should sound
analytical (P6; rc.2 #method-alignment).

Where the tone does not match the authority layer, rewrite it (P6).

## 7. Specification artifact practice

[SPEC_METHOD §2](SPEC_METHOD.md#2-the-chain) is the constitutional
authority for the roles and closure of the specification layers; this
guide supplies the practical writing discipline for those artifacts (P6;
rc.2 #specification-artifact-practice).

When writing a specification artifact (P3, P6):

- state the current live truth, not a narrated transition;
- keep each sentence in its right layer;
- remove stale law, as §9 states; and
- keep design detail out of constitutional layers unless the detail is
  itself constitutional.

A sentence that sounds informative and changes no authority, constraint
or derivability is cut (P2, P6).

## 8. Layer checks

When writing or revising a specification artifact, ask (P2, P6; rc.2
#practical-layer-checks):

1. Can the next downstream layer derive from this?
2. Does this artifact state current truth rather than work in progress?
3. Does any sentence belong in a lower layer instead?

If any answer is wrong, rewrite or delete (P2).

## 9. Current-surface writing

The rule for current-surface writing, with its force, is the
[SPEC_METHOD §2 Specification surface rule](SPEC_METHOD.md#specification-surface-rule):
constitutional specification is written in the present tense, material
that is no longer live is deleted, superseded or moved to commentary, and
an explicit version label is reserved for an immutable release fact, a
selector binding, or clearly historical or superseded material (P3;
rc.2 #current-surface-writing). This guide adds the writing practice:
during a change wave prefer terms such as active, current, base, live,
shared and tenant-local (P3).

# STDO Specification Methodology

Author: Dimitar Popov.

STDO governs purposeful construction through specification, typed composition,
bounded evaluation and authorized disposition.

The [standards library](standards/README.md) is the method entry.
[Foundations](standards/FOUNDATIONS.md) states the premises. The
[transformation library](standards/TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md) defines shared
conditional contracts. Particular methods own their concrete types, policy,
refinements of the single result algebra and authority.

[Responsibility views](standards/README.md#foundations-and-shared-library) project
selected clauses for bounded tasks. Plugin skills route actors to sufficient
material and the exact basis selected by their Product Definition. Views and
skills preserve their owning clauses and confer no operation or decision grant.

The [method interpretation](interpretation/README.md) represents the source
determinations and their dependencies for bounded acquisition. Its source
inventory identifies the document subject; its encoding theory, carrier and
checker have separate coordinates. Structural validation does not establish
semantic fidelity or acceptance. Assessing an explicitly selected source
package does not adopt it as the actor's governing method or install a release.
